items.student_html: A quadratic is $q(x)=(x+1)(x-9)$. The next question asks for its zeros, then its axis of symmetry. Use the factored form to find the zeros and reason from them to the axis of symmetry.
items.student_text: A quadratic is $q(x)=(x+1)(x-9)$. The next question asks for its zeros, then its axis of symmetry. Use the factored form to find the zeros and reason from them to the axis of symmetry.
items.answer_html: The zeros are $-1$ and $\displaystyle 9$. Their midpoint is $\displaystyle 4$, so the axis of symmetry is $x=4$.
